A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same force-shape analysis of UMAP. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and newly added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original embedding experiments, including 100-run initialization studies, learning-rate comparisons, and PubMed classification results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds quantitative force-weight sweeps, ablations, and hybrid embedding experiments.

M1.justification: The original modified attraction, composite attraction, and additive repulsion procedures remain unchanged. Appendix J adds hybrid variants combining attraction and repulsion shapes from different algorithms, with attraction rescaling under the existing UMAP optimizer. The newly derived regularizer interpretations do not themselves change the earlier procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, single-cell transcriptomes, and PubMed embeddings. The new sweeps and hybrids use retained datasets and tasks; the MDS discussion adds no evaluated dataset or application scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds a controlled comparison placing PaCMAP-derived forces alongside UMAP and NEG-t-SNE in Figure 1 and Appendix I, including references with PaCMAP mid-near pairs. Earlier comparisons remain. Parametric UMAP and MDS are analytical additions rather than newly benchmarked empirical baselines.

E3.justification: New experiments independently sweep attraction and repulsion learning rates from 0.1 to 1.0, with annealed and zero-force controls under a shared UMAP optimizer. Trustworthiness uses 10,000 shared sampled indices, while silhouette scores use the complete embedding and Euclidean distances. PaCMAP force sweeps exclude mid-near pairs and provide separate references including them.

E4.justification: Appendix I substantially extends learning-rate sensitivity analysis with two-dimensional sweeps across three datasets, attraction-only and repulsion-only ablations, and PaCMAP mid-near-pair references. Appendix J additionally tests cross-algorithm force combinations and attraction rescaling intended to prevent point flips.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 100-run initialization studies and mean-plus-standard-deviation summaries of pairwise Procrustes distances. The new sweeps and hybrid figures introduce no additional repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds trustworthiness and silhouette heatmaps, force-ablation embeddings, and hybrid results in Figures 18–34. For example, Figure 33(a) newly reports trustworthiness 0.937 and silhouette 0.512. Earlier Procrustes summaries and PubMed accuracies of 49.2% and 55.48% are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 6.1 and its derivation connecting NEG-t-SNE to the modified Parametric UMAP formulation, derives loss regularizers corresponding to the existing force modifications, and extends mathematical analysis to MDS. The original contraction and expansion proofs are retained and relocated to Appendix A.

C1.justification: The central claims about attraction, cluster formation, initialization consistency, and annealing remain. The fifth introductory contribution now includes Parametric UMAP, and the conclusion adds its claimed equivalence to NEG-t-SNE under the specified formulation.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking prevention of point flips to local-structure preservation and identifying a tradeoff with label separation. It also qualifies the confounding effects of changing b, connects them to heavy-tailed kernels, explains MDS behavior, and clarifies that the contraction conditions concern individual updates rather than establishing a learning-rate scheduling rule.

D1.justification: Appendix K identifies the shared UMAP implementation used for the new force-substitution experiments and the scikit-learn metric implementations. Existing nearest-neighbor, initialization, alignment, and package information remains. The statement that reproduction code is attached for review is removed, while the repository link is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused connections to Parametric UMAP and log-sigmoid losses, heavy-tailed kernels, MDS and graph drawing, and newer dimensionality-reduction literature. These broaden supporting relationships while retaining the paper's central positioning as an analysis of attraction and repulsion shapes.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative and much existing prose remain. Targeted revisions reorganize Section 5.2 and streamline Section 6, move graph construction and proofs into appendices, expand appendix navigation, and remove the standalone Impact Statement. Citations change to author-year style.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially expanded, Figure 3 rearranges its experimental panels, and the earlier Figure 5 moves to Appendix F as Figure 11. New heatmaps, extensive embedding grids, MDS curves, and hybrid figures substantially expand the visual presentation. Figure 34(b) has a scaled-UMAP panel label that conflicts with its NEG-t-SNE caption.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its learning-rate argument mainly through selected embedding illustrations. v3 adds controlled independent-force sweeps, quantitative neighborhood and clustering metrics, and ablations across three retained datasets, substantially strengthening evidence for the central mechanism argument. New derivations and explicit discussion of the local-structure/clustering tradeoff improve explanatory value. The Figure 34(b) labeling conflict leaves one hybrid case ambiguous, but this localized reporting issue does not outweigh the broader gains.
